relationship: Enemy overthrow and refusal to rejoice
rationale: The imprecation against enemies and refusal to rejoice at their fall do not on their own settle whether the same occasion, emotion or scope is intended; no harmonization or contradiction claim is retained.

The surrounding sun-and-moon clause and hand-kissing invite this comparison, but Job does not expressly identify the kiss as worship of those bodies. The explicit celestial-worship command is not used to resolve the supplied wording.

Both settings involve threatening angels and acknowledgment of wrong, but the thousand death-bearing angels and the one who will not wound are too distinctive and uncertain to identify with Balaam's encounter or an interpreter.

The supplied without sinning wording must be preserved. The relation of its negatives to Elihu's surrounding accusation is not resolved by importing a familiar edition; no retained equation with the psalm is made.

The preceding unit calls a critic of rulers ungodly, and this relative clause concerns awe and honor before powerful people. Its subject and evaluative force are not securely equated with Deuteronomy's explicit divine impartiality.
